items.title: Traders Short French Bonds as Fight Over Budget Set to Escalate
items.description: Investors are turning bearish on French government bonds, as politicians ready for a fight over the 2027 budget before next year’s presidential election.

items.title: Situational Awareness Sold Taiyo Yuden Shares to Citadel, Others
items.description: Situational Awareness sold shares in Japan’s Taiyo Yuden Co. to Citadel and other investors when it offloaded part of its stake this month, it said in a filing.

items.title: Chinese Companies Slow FX Sales in July as Yuan Support Fades
items.description: Net sales of foreign exchange by Chinese companies fell to a eight-month low in July, suggesting a key source of support for the yuan is fading.

items.title: Japan Five-Year Bond Sale Draws Strongest Demand Since June 2025
items.description: Japan’s five-year government bond auction Tuesday saw the strongest demand since June 2025, as elevated yields underpinned buying.

items.title: Indian Rupee, Bond Bets Retreat as Dollar Swap Window Ends Early
items.description: Caught off-guard by India’s decision to close early a special window to draw foreign-currency deposits, traders are now paring bets on gains in the rupee and short-term bonds.

items.title: Supply Crunch Grips Copper Market as Key Spread Flares Out
items.description: Copper was headed for another day of turbulent trading after a key indicator of short-term supply tightness on the London Metal Exchange spiked.

items.title: Indian IPOs Shine Bright Even as Nifty Loses Momentum
items.description: The primary market is picking up pace, with eight of the past 10 IPOs seeing strong investor demand.

items.title: Yardeni Says Not Pushing Panic Button on Bond Vigilantes Yet
items.description: There’s no reason to panic on the US bond market just yet, even as investors are showing growing signs of unease over rising government debt, according to Yardeni Research.

items.title: Prabowo’s ‘Pragmatic’ Speech Calms Weary Indonesia Investors
items.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto’s annual speech on Friday was a rare uneventful affair, and that’s exactly what investors wanted to hear. Stocks rallied, while bond yields fell.

items.title: Studio Ghibli’s Deepest Secret Is What Comes Next
items.description:
After hits like "Spirited Away" and "The Boy and the Heron," what’s next for Studio Ghibli? 

Sohee Kim explains why the next chapter for Japan’s most celebrated animation studio has yet to be drawn.

items.title: Gold Steadies Near $4,400 on Reduced Expectations for Rate Hike
items.description: Gold steadied near $4,400 an ounce as reduced prospects for an interest-rate hike by the Federal Reserve weighed on the US dollar, making bullion cheaper for most buyers.

items.title: Asian Bonds Follow Treasuries Lower, Oil Gains: Markets Wrap
items.description: Asian bonds followed Treasuries lower as concerns over government finances mounted, while higher oil prices added to fears that inflation will quicken. Stocks declined along with futures.

items.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 18
items.description: Oil gained as prospects for a near-term resolution of the US-Iran war receded, with a fresh vessel attack reported in the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Guggenheim Ties Sink Bonds of $135 Billion Insurer Sammons
items.description: Bonds of Sammons Financial Group fell to the lowest since they were issued in June after a report probed the life insurer’s connections to Mark Walter’s Guggenheim Partners.

items.title: Saudis Offer Oil Near Oman in Possible Sign of Shuttling
items.description: Saudi Arabia is offering to sell oil from off the coast of Oman, a sign that the kingdom may be following the United Arab Emirates in shuttling more barrels through the Strait of Hormuz.
